releases.notes:
- Added Minecraft 26.3 support. Minimum required NeoForge version is 26.3.0.38.
- Robots are now interpolated like everything else (i.e. they move smoothly).
- Robots and blocks that can modify the world now call the exact same functions players do, which allows land claiming/property protection server plugins/mods to stay enforced.
- Stripes pipes and robots now use fluid containers and thrown items on the block in front (1.7.10 feature).
- Stripes pipes and robots also now keep the fluid container after using up contents.
- Stripes pipes now extend their line when fed item pipes, and break minecarts in front of them (1.7.10 feature).
- Builders and Fillers no longer get stuck next to fluids they can't remove, and builds with fluid blocks where there is empty space now complete successfully. In keep-fluid (No-Replace) mode the Builder now waits for nearby moving water before placing torches, snow and other fragile blocks, and places blocks the blueprint wants waterlogged into water of their own kind instead of skipping them. A block that fails to place, from the Builder or a single schematic, no longer deletes the water or lava source, grass, seagrass, snow or flowing water it was placed into. The Builder now breaks a waterlogged block in Replace mode, or a block placed in a spot it was about to fill, like any other wrong block (keeping its drop and contents) instead of building over it; in No-Replace mode it no longer builds over water or lava that flowed in while the block was on its way, and a door, bed or tall plant with either half in water, or a torch or other block standing on a spot it skips for water, is left out instead of keeping the build from ever finishing; it also no longer overwrites a block just outside its area to fit the other half of one the blueprint's edge cut through. Items the Builder or Filler takes back from a cancelled placement are dropped on top of it when its inventory has filled up, instead of disappearing.
- Quarries now repair a frame gap once whatever blocked it is gone (such as a protected area becoming unclaimed).
- Mining Wells and Pumps no longer delete waterlogged blocks.
- Idle Pumps over huge pools and the Zone Planner map aren't performance hogs any more.
- Improved the performance of Robot pathfinding and pipe wires.
- Pipe wires now show their state to players who walk into range or rejoin without a large chunk reload.
- The Flood Gate now fills from a bounded search around itself instead of scanning an entire lake.
- Pumps and robots no longer load or generate chunks while searching, pathing, or draining.
- Machines keep or drop their contents correctly when blown up or replaced by commands.
- Stacks above 99 (from mods that raise stack limits) are no longer lost when saved in pipes, Assembly Tables, Builders, item lists or robot requests.
- Fluid pipes no longer create free fluid when another mod test-fills them and then cancels the transfer.
- {1.21.1} /setblock, /fill and /clone no longer spill contents when breaking machines (matches the newer MC versions).
- Fixed the Distiller so that it now drops the items in its container slots.
- The Electronic Library no longer rejects blueprints holding pistons or blocks with replaceable variants. Older saved blueprints will be repaired automatically.
- Fixed an edge case in the Guide Book where text would render over page numbers, and links that wrap onto the next page are now clickable on both pages.
- The guide book's Sort By System button has its own icon instead of the old Sort By Mod one.
- {1.21.1} Page icons and link underlines no longer show through the guide book's Chapters list on small windows.
- {1.21.10/1.21.11/26.1/26.1.1/26.1.2/26.2} Fixed Fragile Fluid Shards showing the wrong color for colored fluids (lava shards looked blue) on Minecraft 1.21.10 and newer.
- The Wooden Diamond pipe's filter modes are now called Allowlist and Blocklist since that is easier to translate.

releases.notes:
- **ROBOTS!!** Fully back for for the first time since Minecraft 1.7.10, with a rudimentary in-game guide through the Guide Book
- Added a complete Simplified Chinese (`zh_cn`) translation (machine assisted), thank you for starting it, [beizhou1](https://github.com/beizhou1)!  
  - 如发现翻译不准确，请提交拉取请求或反馈问题
- You can now fully disable BuildCraft's own facades from ever existing/generating in the Common mod config now (in case other mods add facades). Thank you for the suggestion, [MapperTV](https://github.com/MapperTV)!
- Adjusted/fixed how blocks look in the hand (and rotated the Distiller to face foreward in the inventory)
- Updated the Distiller GUI to be more representative of what tank is responsible for when production has stopped
- Fixed various issues with blocks not remembering data (such as fuel for the Stirling engine, who owns a Filler block, fluid states of the Builder)
- Made data handling within the Electronic Library far more robust
- Quarries no longer freeze forever when their frame area holds bedrock or a protected block (such as bedrock or a block you don't own)
- Mining Wells and Pumps no longer delete the water they drill through
- Improvements to how Builders in Clear fluid mode handle edge cases
- Brought back the "sort by mod" option in the Guide Book (it now sorts by internal subsystem, equivalent to the old submod method)
- Fixed some one off bad links and old formatting for Guide Book pages
- Non-BuildCraft fluids (i.e. other modded fluids) now no longer show up as a missing texture within BuildCraft storage containers 
- All buttons have been unified to be based off of Vanilla's own button class, meaning resource packs now affect them
- Redstone engines no longer feed Forge Energy machines when MJ-to-RF autoconversion is on (stolen from upstream 8.0.1)
- Tanks, Chutes, Filtered Buffers and Requesters drive redstone comparators again
- Advancements earned through a Stripes pipe/robot now go to the owner on every Minecraft version (broken on 1.21.1 and 26.2)
- Builders no longer wait forever to place waterloggable blocks next to water, or to place water and lava blocks once fluid is piped into their tanks
- Mining blocks now actually handle waterlogged blocks the way one might expect them to
- The snapshot (Templates/Blueprints) list in the Electronic Library are now sorted by alphanumeric order, and usability of the list has been improved
- Facades now add a degree of explosion resistance to pipes like they did in 1.12.2
- Water gel respects mining-speed and harvest effects from other mods (shoutouts to those who actually use this item)
- (1.21.10/1.21.11) Stirling engine gives back the correct leftover container for modded fuels whose leftover depends on the item
- Path & volume markers can be placed within some fluids now and no longer break next to them
- Pumps also respect waterlogged blocks the way you'd expect them to
- Heavy oil no longer voids waterlogged blocks (the whole waterlogging system has been my bane)
- Speed improvements for blocks that interact directly with the world (such as Builders and Mining blocks), especially on 1.21.1
- Distiller and Heat Exchanger no longer re-save their chunk every few ticks while stuck with a container they can't use
- The Power Tester block (an infinite MJ sink) is now available in creative mode/via cheats instead of only being accessible for mod developers
- Made it harder for me to ship a .jar with missing resources (please open an issue if any textures are broken)
- Made it so that blocks broken by BuildCraft that have vines on them don't leave the vines in the air
- Made it so that if your NeoForge is up-to-date, oil now breaks your fall as you'd hope
- Added the mod icon to 26.2's new mod screen
- (1.21.1) Fixed BuildCraft fluids rendering scaled up in item form
- Gate parameter slots that hold an item can be filled in again, which is imperative for robots to work

releases.notes:
- Fixed a crash when opening certain guide pages. Thank you for your crash log, [Ryk7039](https://github.com/Ryk7039)!
- Machines now update chunks a lot less often (this should improve performance)
- Updated code relating to how spectators can view machine GUIs
- Auto Workbench now correctly accepts FE when the BuildCraft config is set for machines to use FE
- RF/FE and MJ pipes now share the same rendering code, so any visual bugs that were exclusive to RF/FE pipes should be gone
- Editing a volume defined by a volume box or land markers now only updates that volume instead of every single one in the loaded dimension
- Items ejected from pipes into an inventory now top up partially-filled stacks before starting new ones, matching every other BuildCraft item output.
- Made the Oil generation code far more sensible; fixes multiple sources of freezes/server hangs on 1.21.1. Thank you for investigation, [MapperTV](https://github.com/MapperTV)!
- **Updated the NeoForge minimums:** 1.21.1 is now 21.1.151+, 1.21.10 is now 21.10.63+

releases.notes:
- {1.21.1} Fixed a crash when breaking a Distiller. Thank you for your report, [Ryk7039](https://github.com/Ryk7039)!
- **Items travelling through pipes no longer lose their enchantments, custom names, or damage when the chunk is saved and reloaded**
- Builders and Fillers now reach their full building speed once their internal power buffer is half full, instead of permanently topping out at half speed even on a completely full buffer
- Fixed three of BuildCraft's four JEI plugins sharing one identifier, which could cause JEI to drop some of the mod's recipes
- Fixed FE/RF pipes not rendering their power sometimes (MJ was fixed the same way previous update)
- Fixed engines occasionally forgetting their recorded owner if they were placed and then never interacted with before their area unloaded
- Fixed the collapsible info/help ledgers flying up off the top of the screen when collapsed
- Fixed a "Network Protocol Error" disconnect when right-clicking certain machines while in spectator mode
- Blocks with status lights now stop rendering those lights when obscured by another block
- Improvements to the 3D preview of blueprints
- "Map Location" item and "Zone Planner" block are now available in survival. They don't really do all that much yet.
- Idle quarries no longer are a performance hog
